scope: CPU subprocess client tests plus read-only comparison against current draft p198 native protocol source; no native compilation/execution, device, service or HTTP action.

resolved_finding.problem: Restored request completion previously accepted visible history shorter than submitted input plus emitted tokens.
resolved_finding.fix: Require visible_tokens >= len(input)+len(emitted) for every request; retain equality for fresh requests.

reviewed_checks: RUN cannot embed immediate save; each completed request blocks next RUN until explicit SAVE or RELEASE.
Ready admission validates v2 protocol, context, vocabulary, one model load and equal request/control budgets.
Token sequence, completion identity/count/quiescence and pending request/processed/visible/pending-token descriptor are checked.
Local malformed save inputs do not consume pending state; operation IDs cannot repeat.
SAVE acknowledgement validates checkpoint identity, root-relative path scope, operation receipt, manifest digest syntax and unchanged pending descriptor.
Final request remains awaiting disposition; successful final SAVE or RELEASE transitions to draining without another QUIT.
Explicit close can discard an unresolved pending request only when terminal receipt reports that exact pending request and discard state.
Terminal completed request/control counts and safe exit are required, followed by zero process exit.
Event deadlines are checked even for buffered events; transport/control failures halt later intake and retain process for coordinator drain.
Current p198 source emits expected field names/types; full submitted SAVE history is compared with retained native processed tokens and pending token.
limitations: Native p198 source is still under preparation; these hashes identify the reviewed draft, not compiled or device-qualified behavior.
Client cannot independently authenticate a manifest hash against filesystem contents; a save caller must verify the retained native receipt/manifest when integrating storage policy.
No general parking policy, HTTP service, OpenAI compatibility, concurrency or device qualification is claimed.
